html:
Demosthenes was an Athenian statesman and orator, born in 384 BCE, who spent his career urging Athens to stand up to Philip II of Macedon. He is often called the greatest orator of ancient Greece.

His father died when he was seven, and his guardians wasted his inheritance. He trained himself to speak, according to Plutarch, by talking with pebbles in his mouth and over the noise of the sea, then sued the guardians. He earned a living writing speeches for others, some about Pasion's bank.

From 351 BCE his Philippics warned that Philip meant to swallow Greece. He built the alliance between Athens and Thebes that fought Macedon at the Battle of Chaeronea in 338 BCE, where he served in the ranks. Later his speech On the Crown defended his life's work against his rival Aeschines.

In 324 BCE he was convicted of taking bribes and went into exile. He came back to lead the revolt after Alexander died, the Lamian War. When it failed, he fled the Macedonian general Antipater and took poison in 322 BCE. Cicero later named his speeches against Mark Antony "Philippics" after his.
sum: Demosthenes was an Athenian statesman and orator, born in 384 BCE, who spent his career urging Athens to stand up to Philip II of Macedon. He is often called the greatest orator of ancient Greece.
